messages:
drew: follow-up from yesterday's pinning design session. i wanted to capture a few unresolved tradeoffs around semantics for ttl/expiry, rollback signalling, and namespace collisions when tenants use their own version ids.

ines: main concern is semantics drift across runtimes. if one runtime treats missing ttl as infinite and another treats it as short-lived, we'll see surprising evictions. propose a single canonical default: missing `e` means indefinite (no-auto-evict) and servers must only evict on explicit `evict` action or expired `e`.

mike: agree on default, but we need a safe-mode for emergency mass-evict: control-plane can submit a top-level `evict_all` marker in expanded admin schema. hot-path wire must not include this flag.

drew: on namespace collisions: tenants sometimes use semantic version strings that mirror our internal release tags. suggestion: require `v` to be namespaced (prefix with model id) OR include an optional `ns` short key in compact wire schema. which is less painful?

ines: prefer adding `ns` short key. tiny overhead but avoids ambiguous lookups. server will fallback to default namespace when `ns` missing to maintain backward compat.

mike: rollback signalling: need a small `rb` flag (boolean) that marks this pin as a rollback anchor so fallback logic can prefer earlier model variants. `rb` should be control-plane/admin-only; not in hot-path by default. but could be present in wire for canary orchestrations.

drew: runtime race conditions: if two pin updates arrive concurrently, we need clear ordering. recommend server reject concurrent writes without monotonic `seq` integer. add `s` short field as sequence number; server enforces monotonicity per (ns,v) tuple.

ines: telemetry: include `obs` list for observer ids and `src` for actor id (who created the pin). small fields, high debug value. also record `reason` in admin logs only.

mike: sketch compact wire example: `{"p":"hard","k":"model","v":"m:20261101-9f","ns":"tenant-42","e":"2027-01-01T00:00:00Z","s":42,"sv":4,"obs":["edge-3"],"src":"deploy-api"}`

drew: compatibility rules: servers must ignore unknown fields; clients must not assume server will accept `s` gaps (server may enforce strict monotonic sequences). when `sv` >= 4 we enable sequence enforcement. older clients without `sv` continue with eventual-last-write semantics.

ines: control-plane admin schema will accept `evict_all`, `reason`, `overrides` and `rb` fields. control-plane will expand compact fields into verbose equivalents when storing in db and when showing in Console.

audit-bot: created ticket PIN-900 for sequence enforcement tests and PIN-901 for namespace migration guide.

drew: decision summary: adopt compact wire with short keys including new `ns`, `s`(seq), and `obs` fields; default expiry semantics = indefinite; control-plane supports richer admin-only fields (`evict_all`, `reason`, `overrides`, `rb`); require `sv` for feature gating of sequence enforcement. action items: mike -> add seq logic + tests; ines -> doc defaults and migration notes; drew -> PR for serializer and runtime helpers.

mike: will start seq test harness and open PR this week.

ines: will draft migration doc and examples.

drew: thanks all :thumbsup: will track follow-ups in PIN-900 and PIN-901.
